A valid plan is retained as validated with a CLEAN plan artifact (application/json, retention class plan-artifact); a malformed plan or capability mismatch is retained as validation_failed with every unsupported item explained. 202.description: A validated composition plan was rendered through the deterministic AE worker into one retained 9:16 final MP4, thumbnail and captions. The render preserved the plan input hash and capability version and validated the worker output (codec, duration, resolution, golden output hash) before retaining any final media. A versioned FinalVideo (CURRENT) was retained with an immutable revision lineage: a new revision superseded the prior current video without overwriting it. The final-video sha256 is the deterministic golden render hash, so the same plan renders to the same hash across revisions. A render-level CreativeLineage row ties the final video back through the composition instruction, AE plan, render attempt and the copied G5 generated-asset ancestry; a revision creates a new immutable lineage row for the new final video. The render attempt logs and final media are retained CLEAN Artifacts. Render is a costly, externally visible mutation, so an Idempotency-Key is required and scoped to the exact render operation input (composition instruction, AE plan, plan canonical hash, input asset hashes, capability version); the same key replayed against a different composition returns IDEMPOTENCY_INPUT_CONFLICT. The input hash, asset hashes, signed URLs and raw worker payloads never reach the browser.

202.description: The approved scheduled calendar post was published to the provider bound to its platform (Meta or YouTube Shorts) exactly once. The provider is derived server-side from the calendar post's platform; the request carries no provider field. A durable PublishOperation is persisted before network I/O; the operation binds the workspace, calendar post, provider route, idempotency key and a server-side request hash, and stores the external post id and public post URL only once the provider identity is known. A YouTube upload that is accepted but still processing returns the operation in processing while the post stays accepted; a callback or reconciliation later drives it to completed. A timeout after possible acceptance returns unknown and the post stays submitting; the caller must reconcile before retry. An Idempotency-Key is required; the same key replayed with the same input returns the same operation (replay true) and never calls the provider again. The request hash is never surfaced; no secret, signed URL, object key or credential leaks. The simulator surfaces a signed callback envelope (x-meta-signature or x-youtube-signature) carrying the public post URL for the deterministic test to post back.

A replay of an already-verified post surfaces the same PostVerification and the same logical notification with replay true and duplicateCollapsed true; no second notification or snapshot is created. The manual live URL, when supplied, is bound to the calendar post. No secret, signed URL, object key, recipient user id, payload hash or raw provider payload leaks.

No completion notification, evidence artifact or performance snapshot is created while processing.

200.description: The complete creative lineage for one final video as a bounded, redacted, hash-manifested ancestry export. The export anchors on the immutable CreativeLineage row and traverses the approved brand profile, selected script, consent-safe avatar, estimate, provider operation, generated asset, composition instruction, AE plan, render attempt, final video, calendar post, audience verification and the initial performance observation. status is complete when every ancestry record is present, incomplete when ancestry is missing (named in missing), and blocked when the final-video sha256 no longer matches the retained render attempt output hash (named in mismatches). Cost attribution (provider total, authorized maximum, currency, price version), source and provider timestamps are surfaced as observations. A stable manifestSha256 binds the canonical ancestry. No secret, signed URL, object key, raw provider payload, external id, request hash, idempotency key, source hash or cross-workspace reference leaks; each artifact entry carries its public content sha256 and never its object key.

The observation window starts where the prior snapshot ended and ends now. No secret, signed URL, object key, raw provider payload, account id or source hash leaks; the metrics are observations of past platform state, never a forecast, projection or promise of reach, virality, conversion or causal performance.

200.description: Verified publishing callback acknowledged; the publish operation transitioned exactly once and the calendar post advanced in lockstep. The {provider} path selects the signature header (meta: x-meta-signature, youtube: x-youtube-signature). A publish.processing event keeps the operation in processing while the post stays accepted; a publish.completed event binds the public post URL and advances the post to published_unverified. Duplicate callbacks produce one transition (duplicate true) and never write a second time.
